aspects.says: The permitted list is kept in the class file, and the JVM refuses to load a subtype compiled before the sealing with IncompatibleClassChangeError.
basis: section:The JVM Checks the List When It Loads a Subtype

aspects.says: Without a permits clause, the permitted subtypes are those declared in the same source file, never the rest of the package.
basis: section:Without permits, the Subtypes in the Same File Are the List

aspects.says: A sealed type's permits clause names its direct subtypes, and javac refuses any other, anonymous classes and lambdas included.
basis: section:A Sealed Type Names Its Direct Subtypes, and javac Refuses Any Other

aspects.says: getPermittedSubclasses() returns only the direct subtypes, so code that needs every concrete type walks down through each sealed subtype, and it returns null for a type that isn't sealed.
basis: section:At Run Time, getPermittedSubclasses() Lists the Direct Subtypes Only

aspects.says: A permitted record qualifies as it is, while a permitted class needs final, sealed or non-sealed.
basis: section:A Sealed Type Names Its Direct Subtypes, and javac Refuses Any Other
aspects.reason: a rule javac enforces has no wrong solution that compiles, and the three modifiers are practised in unit 2.5.2, which teaches them
